<title>Wallet has no did:web identity removal flow (UI gated to did:plc; backend would wedge on the PLC tombstone if ungated)</title>
<description>
Found during the <issue id="325ad336-792b-4581-9e45-c162dd9e26ba" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-395/migrate-didwebmalperciodev-to-production-staging-rehearsal-first-live">MM-395</issue> rehearsal (see `docs/validation/2026-07-24-mm-395-didweb-migration-rehearsal.md`): the wallet's permanent identity removal is did:plc-only end to end. This is the same defect class as the six rehearsal bugs — did:plc assumptions ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) + tombstone op) in a surface that should be method-aware — caught here by inspection before it could bite live.

## Current state

**UI (the actual user-visible gap):** `+page.svelte` gates the entry point on `selectedDid?.startsWith('did:plc:')`, so `DIDDocumentScreen` never renders the "Remove this identity…" button for a did:web. A did:web identity cannot be removed from the wallet's removal flow at all — the gate is correct defensively, because of what sits behind it:

**Backend (latent wedge, currently unreachable from the UI):** `confirm_identity_removal` runs `deleteAccount` first (method-agnostic, would succeed), then `tombstone_and_wipe`, which fetches the DID's **[plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) audit log** for the tombstone `prev` — a 404 for any did:web. The tombstone never submits, the local wipe (gated behind tombstone success) never runs, and the pending-removal marker never clears: the account would be gone (single-use email code spent) while the wallet re-offers a doomed "tombstone pending, retry" on every launch, forever. Unreachable today only because the UI gate exists; the raw IPC command has no did:web guard of its own.

Meanwhile the only did:web affordance is `forget_identity_locally` (local wipe, no server deletion) — designed as the escape hatch for foreign/dead accounts, not as a first-party removal flow.

## What "deletion" means for a did:web

There is no PLC tombstone. A did:web dies when its document leaves the domain — an **operator action outside the wallet's control** (delete/blank `https://<host>/.well-known/did.json`, or serve 410). So the did:web removal flow is:

1. `requestAccountDelete` / `deleteAccount` (unchanged, method-agnostic),
2. **no PLC tombstone leg** — no tombstone marker semantics, no retry state,
3. local Keychain wipe,
4. UI: tell the user the last step is theirs — take the `did.json` down to retire the DID network-wide, with the same "the wallet can't do this part for you" framing the did:web ceremony's publish step already uses.

`RemovalOutcome.tombstone_cid` becomes optional (or a variant) — there is no CID to report.

## Suggested shape

* Backend first: branch `confirm_identity_removal`/`tombstone_and_wipe` on `did:web:` (mirror of the `finalize_migration` branch from PR #420) — did:web → deleteAccount → wipe, never touching [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>). Also guard the raw command so an ungated caller can't reproduce the wedge.
* Then ungate the UI: drop the `did:plc:` condition on `onremove` and give `RemoveIdentityScreen` a did:web epilogue ("remove your did.json to finish retiring the DID") instead of the tombstone progress state.
* Unit tests: did:web removal never calls [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>); wipe ordering preserved; the wedge regression (marker cleared without a tombstone; no permanent retry state).

## Traceability

* Rehearsal record: `docs/validation/2026-07-24-mm-395-didweb-migration-rehearsal.md` ("every did:plc assumption broke on did:web contact" — this is the next instance)
* Sibling fixes for the same class: PR #418 (ceremony key encoding), #419 (path detection), #420 (discover_pds + finalize), #422 (service-id parsing)
* Immediate practical relevance: <issue id="325ad336-792b-4581-9e45-c162dd9e26ba" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-395/migrate-didwebmalperciodev-to-production-staging-rehearsal-first-live">MM-395</issue> cleanup wants the throwaway `did:web:rehersal-production.up.railway.app` account deleted on production. With no wallet flow, cleanup goes through the admin surface (server-side deletion) + `forget_identity_locally` on the device — which is fine, and this ticket is what makes the first-party path exist for real users.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

MM-464 is done and in review: **[PR #425](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/425)**, linked on the Linear issue.

## What the fix is

The ticket called this a latent wedge, and that framing shaped the implementation. The did:plc-only assumption sat in `tombstone_and_wipe`, which is reached by **two** commands: `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` — the resume path the pending-removal marker routes to on every launch. So the branch went into a new shared core, `retire_and_wipe`, rather than at the command boundary:

- **did:plc** → unchanged tombstone-then-wipe, wipe-last ordering invariant intact.
- **anything else** → straight to the local wipe, never touching plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`.

Guarding only the entry point would have satisfied the UI but left an ungated caller able to reproduce the wedge — and, more importantly, would have left the *resume* path still able to loop forever against a directory that never hosted the DID.

On the frontend I dropped the `did:plc:` gate on `onremove`, and `RemoveIdentityScreen` now branches on the outcome's null `tombstoneCid` — the backend's own report that nothing was published — rather than re-deriving the method from the DID string. A did:web removal drops the "retire on the network by tombstoning" promise, withholds the escape hatch's advanced "also retire on the network" option (it could not do what it says), and ends in a `web_epilogue` naming the exact `did.json` URL to take down.

One thing worth flagging: I checked the PDS side rather than guessing at the copy. `serve_hosted_did_document` JOINs the `accounts` row, so for a **Custos-hosted** did:web, deleting the account already stops the document being served — there's nothing left for the user to do. The epilogue says both cases explicitly instead of sending someone hunting for a file they don't host.

## Verification

Rust tests (16 passed, including a catch-all mock asserting **zero** plc.directory calls and the wedge regression), clippy clean on touched code, `pnpm check` 0 errors, 158 frontend tests, and the docs/changelog/ticket-ref gates. I also drove the whole flow in the browser harness against the `rekey-mixed` scenario's `did:web:web.example.com` — screenshot of the epilogue is in the PR description's verification section — and re-confirmed the did:plc path is unchanged (tombstone bullet present, no epilogue, straight back to the list).

Two clippy warnings remain in `blob_backup.rs`; they're pre-existing on `main` and that file isn't touched by this branch, so I left them alone rather than widening the diff.
